steps.say: Many plants make flowers, but not all of them do. Ferns and mosses do not have flowers.
The petals are often bright. They help attract insects. Green sepals protect the flower when it is a bud.
The stamen is the male part. It has an anther on top that makes pollen, held up by a filament.
The carpel is the female part. It has a sticky stigma on top, a style, and an ovary at the bottom that holds the ovules.
After pollination and fertilisation, the ovules become seeds and the ovary grows into a fruit.

check.prompt: Which part of a flower makes pollen?
hints: It is part of the stamen.
It sits on top of the filament.

check.prompt: Which part of a flower catches pollen?
hints: It is at the top of the carpel.
check.explanation: The stigma is sticky, so it catches pollen.
